newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle strength seen muted by report.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle strength seen muted by report.

text.p: Expected strength in U.S. Plains fed cattle prices from firm beef values next week was seen muted by Friday's USDA monthly cattle on feed report, which was termed bearish to CME cattle futures, sources said.

USDA reported July placements in seven major states at 118 percent of a year ago, much higher than the average pre-report analysts' estimate of 100.8 percent and well above the highest analyst estimate of 106.5 percent.
On-feed supplies as of August 1 were pegged at 119 percent, above the average estimate of 115.6, and July marketings were put at 109, above the average of 105.5 percent.
"We may not get that $67.00 we were hoping to see next week," one Texas Panhandle feedlot manager said. "It could even hold prices steady."
Cattle owners were seen pricing cattle at $66.00 on Monday, with bids expected at $64.00 to $65.00, several feedlot sources said.

Active buying this week at $65.00 brought prices back to last week's early top before weak sales pulled prices down to $64.00 late last week. Trading this week was so brisk that most showlists were sold out. The Kansas market on Wednesday had the second largest single day volume on record.
